GEOMETRY — subordinate only to the product invariants.
Use Image 1 for the product's exact appearance, view and pixel size; its initial x-y is a starting location that may remain or change by one rigid translation. Apply the product-placement and recomposed-support policy below.
DIAGNOSTIC OCCUPANCY: HIGH-FILL/CLOSE. Occupancy does not change placement permission. For every camera view, keep the product at its initial x-y or use one optional rigid image-plane x-y translation for a usable composition. Preserve exact pixel width and height and every other product invariant. Never resize, reorient, reproject, redraw, crop, or occlude the product. Independently recompose support and room beneath or around the final product position; product and support need not move together.

Translate the laptop horizontally left as one rigid piece until its leftmost silhouette has a narrow, comfortable margin from the frame; keep its vertical position unchanged. This opens roughly the right third of the picture for a clear planning surface. Independently construct a pale wood worktable beneath it, extending beyond both side edges of the photograph. Fully support the base, with a small usable gap to the near working edge and generous wood surface behind and beside it. The front edge runs below the laptop, rising gently toward the right; depth edges recede toward the upper left. Place the working chair in the near-left foreground, aligned with the keyboard, mostly cropped below the frame and entirely below the product silhouette. Keep the approach free of other furnishings.

Camera: Use a close, nearly frontal view from slightly above table height, looking gently downward with a level camera and restrained telephoto perspective. Preserve exactly the laptop's existing view of the screen, keyboard and chassis; the leftward translation does not change its projection or pixel size. Build the table and room around those fixed edge directions, with a shared horizon. Show a little space between the laptop base and the table's near edge, then a small cropped portion of the working chair below it.

Composition: The fully visible laptop occupies the left and middle of the close modern office scene after one horizontal translation, leaving a broad empty planning area on the pale wood worktable at mid-right. The table supports the entire base with natural contact and believable clearances; its near edge faces the keyboard. A cream woven upholstered chair sits at near-left, aligned with the keyboard and pulled back enough for access. To reconcile seating with the close framing and mandatory product visibility, show only its upper back below the tabletop, cropped by the bottom edge rather than crossing the laptop. A ribbed glass partition stands at far-right behind the table, anchored to the floor outside the crop. A dusty blue matte-painted wall spans the far-plane upper-left and upper-center background as a broad visible band above the screen. Soft daylight enters from the right through the partition, with generous neutral fill and gentle warm wood tones. No requested object is omitted; the chair's visibility is adapted to prevent occlusion.

TRANSLATION-ONLY PRODUCT PLACEMENT; RECOMPOSED SUPPORT
For every camera view, including close/high-fill views, keep the product at its initial location or reposition it using only one rigid image-plane x-y translation when that improves usable composition. This changes position only, not the product view or size.

Preserve product identity, exact pixel width and height, yaw, pitch, roll, viewing angle, visible faces, camera-facing surfaces, projection, perspective, foreshortening, silhouette proportions, state, finish, details, logo, display content and full visibility. Independently recompose support and room beneath or around the final product position; product and support need not move together. Do not move the product merely to center it or make it more prominent.

Preserve exact product pixel width and height and every other product invariant. Never shrink, enlarge, zoom, reframe, rotate, reproject, or crop the product to make a move feasible. Where translation is allowed, if a move cannot preserve every invariant, retain the initial x-y coordinates instead.

The only permitted product change is one rigid image-plane x-y translation. Keep its exact pixel width and height, yaw, pitch, roll, viewing angle, visible faces, camera-facing surfaces, perspective, projection, foreshortening, silhouette, aspect proportions, open/closed and powered state, finish, details, logo and display content. Do not rotate, mirror, resize, shear, warp, reproject, redraw or activate the product. Do not zoom, reframe or change the viewpoint in a way that alters the product.

At the chosen product position, compose a category- and scenario-appropriate support beneath its weight-bearing base. The support may change independently of the product's translation: do not preserve baseline product-to-edge distances, tabletop extents or absolute support-edge locations as requirements. Fully support the base without floating or overhang, with believable front, back and side clearances, natural weight-bearing contact, a contact shadow and material-appropriate reflections on the support.

Construct furniture around the unchanged product orientation. A printer must sit square to its support in 3D with usable access to its operating front. A laptop must face a usable seating or working edge with clear access to its keyboard and display. Do not rotate the product or reveal a different face to fit the furniture. Support axes, room perspective, horizon and vanishing geometry must be compatible with the unchanged product projection at its chosen position; do not retain incompatible geometry from the initial layout.

Keep exactly one product, entirely inside the frame and fully visible. No prop, furniture edge or foreground object may occlude it. Remove the gray guide, diagram marks and any ghost or duplicate product. If the product moves, complete the vacated location as part of the scene. If a candidate placement violates any product or support requirement, choose another placement or recompose the support and room without relaxing the product invariants.

GUIDE LEGEND: Image 1 is the current canvas to edit. Its real product pixels establish the exact product appearance, view and pixel size to preserve. Their frame position may remain unchanged or change by one rigid x-y translation. The flat gray region and its boundaries show an initial support plan, not output pixels or required support edges, distances or extents. At the chosen product position, compose an appropriate support beneath the unchanged product. Remove all gray-guide and diagram remnants, any duplicate product and any product-shaped remnant at the initial location. Keep only one intact product at the final location. Render the lighting, palette, materials and textures described here photographically. When blue is unspecified, include one large blue surface/furnishing or multiple clearly visible blue elements whose combined area makes blue immediately noticeable, not a token accent. Tiny props, thin partition frames, screen graphics, sky and lighting casts alone do not qualify. Keep the planned blue materials, visible extent and placement consistent; leave small props neutral by default. Explicit minimal-blue or no-blue requests override that default, as do explicit blue amounts or carriers. Keep the product's original color, finish, exact orientation/view, scale, details and full visibility. Every camera view permits only one optional rigid image-plane x-y translation. Never change the product or its camera viewpoint to make room for blue. Retain requested warm-neutral lighting alongside physical blue materials. Do not impose a universal blue hue or coverage percentage. Match soft, uniform exposure and gentle contrast; no bright-hero/dark-room treatment and no orange or global blue color cast. The product pixels in Image 1 control all product details, including any unlit display. Never reproduce any diagram lines, boxes, labels, text or flat guide colors.

Turn Image 1 into a photograph; preserve the laptop's exact orientation/view, pixel size and details; only its x-y position may change. Preserve exact product pixel width and height and every other invariant; never shrink, enlarge, zoom, reframe, rotate, reproject, or crop the product to make a move feasible; where translation is allowed, retain initial x-y if a move cannot preserve every invariant.

Build a pale wood worktable independently beneath the final position, fully supporting the base with natural contact shadow, no overhang, a small front working gap and ample back/side clearance. Crop furniture, not the laptop. The working edge faces the keyboard, rising gently rightward; depth recedes upper-left. Use soft right-side daylight, generous neutral fill, gentle contrast and visible wood grain.

One full-bleed photorealistic photograph with natural imperfections; no added text, logos, borders, watermark or CGI look.
